Conceptual and mathematical models are often used to represent complex and unconstrained hydrologic environments (Neuman 2003).
Model parameter values for numerical calculations are often not a direct physical interpretation and can rarely be measured in the field.

Consequently, models are calibrated using objective functions (e.g., Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency [NSE], root mean squared error [RMSE], peak discharge) and the "best" model structure and parameter set or sets are often selected to represent a given process or system of processes (Wagner et al. 2001).
Previous studies have called for the adoption of reproducibility and transparency within hydrology to add credibility to scientific claims.

Difficulties frequently arise in model performance evaluation due to multiple interpretations of output or data products, differing mathematical descriptions of underlying processes, and uncertainties present in the input and parameter datasets (Kavestski et al. 2006; Hutton et al. 2016).
